user.title: Connect to the Envisalink
user.description: Enter the connection details for your Envisalink EVL-3/EVL-4 module. The Envisalink admits one TPI client at a time, so disable any other Envisalink integration first.

data_description.host: The Envisalink's IP address or hostname on your LAN. Give it a DHCP reservation; a changed address means reconfiguring.
data_description.port: The TPI port. 4025 unless you changed it on the Envisalink's web page.
data_description.password: The password for the Envisalink's local web page, not a panel code.
data_description.panel_model: The alarm panel behind the Envisalink. It sets the zone and partition limits and, for field programming, which keystroke grammar is used and how much of it is verified.
data_description.user_code: Optional. A panel user code Home Assistant will type to arm and disarm when a call does not supply one. Leaving it blank means every arm and disarm needs a code. It can be changed or removed later in the options.
data_description.num_partitions: How many partitions the panel has configured (1 to 8). One alarm control panel entity is created per partition.
data_description.num_zones: How many zones to create sensors for (1 to 250, within the model's limit). Unused zones simply stay closed.

reauth_confirm.title: Envisalink password rejected
reauth_confirm.description: The Envisalink at {host} rejected the stored password. Enter the current one.

data_description.password: The password for the Envisalink's local web page.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the Envisalink at that host and port. If another Envisalink integration or app is connected, it holds the only TPI session.
error.too_many_zones: That is more zones than the selected panel model supports.
error.too_many_partitions: That is more partitions than the selected panel model supports.

init.title: Envisalink Field Programmer options
init.description: Codes are never shown here. Default user code: {user_code_state}. Installer code: {installer_code_state}. Leave a code field blank to keep the stored code; tick its remove switch to clear it.

data.remove_user_code: Remove the stored default user code

data_description.user_code: A panel user code Home Assistant types to arm and disarm when a call does not supply one. With one set, the alarm panel entity disarms without asking anyone for a code.
data_description.remove_user_code: Clears the stored default user code, so every arm and disarm needs a code again.
data_description.installer_code: Enables the field-programming actions. Every guided action types this code followed by 800 to open Program Mode. Leave it unset if you never program the panel from Home Assistant; arming, disarming and bypass never use it.
data_description.remove_installer_code: Clears the stored installer code and disables field programming.
data_description.keepalive_interval: Seconds between keepalive polls that detect a silently dead connection (10 to 300). Zone state is refreshed every 30 seconds regardless.

entry_not_found.message: No Envisalink Field Programmer entry has the id {entry_id}.

not_loaded.message: {name} is not loaded, so this action cannot run.

cannot_connect.message: Could not connect to the Envisalink at {host}: {error}

invalid_auth.message: The Envisalink at {host} rejected the stored password.

no_code.message: No user code was given and no default user code is configured. A Vista panel has no code-free way to arm or disarm.

empty_keystrokes.message: No keystrokes were given. There is nothing to send to the panel.

invalid_keystroke_characters.message: Invalid keystroke characters: {characters}. A keypad accepts only digits, * and #.

opens_program_mode.message: Refusing to send {keys}: on this panel that sequence opens installer Program Mode, which governs every data field including fire zones and UL-listing-relevant settings, and this protocol cannot read back what is on the keypad display. Set confirm_installer_risk to true if you intend it.

keystrokes_not_accepted.message: The Envisalink did not accept the keystroke sequence: {error}

no_installer_code.message: Field programming needs an installer code. Set one in this integration's options (Settings > Devices & services > Envisalink Field Programmer > Configure) first.

guided_op_unsupported.message: Guided {operation} programming is not available for {model}. {note}

unverified_model.message: {model} is not verified against its own programming guide ({verification}): {notes} Field numbers and zone type codes may be wrong for this exact panel, and this integration cannot read the panel back to catch a mistake. Set confirm_unverified_model to true to proceed anyway, then check the result at the keypad.

life_safety_zone_type.message: Zone type {zone_type} ({label}) is a life-safety type. Set confirm_life_safety to true to confirm you intend it. This integration cannot read back what type the zone is now, so check at the keypad (installer code, then # and 56) if you are not certain.

invalid_timing_field.message: Timing field {field} is not valid for {model}. Valid fields: {valid}.

invalid_timing_value.message: That timing value is out of range: {error}
